headline: The trials behind
the peptides.
dek: BPC-157, TB-500 and KPV can now be compounded. The human research is thin.
byline: Adonis Men’s Health · Checked Oct 31, 2026 · Clinical review pending

glance.label: Human studies
glance.line: BPC-157: five, about 80 people. TB-500: one 3-person case report. KPV: none.

glance.label: Compounding allowed
glance.line: All three, under HHS conditions since Oct 30, 2026. Not approval.

glance.label: Sport bans
glance.line: BPC-157 (S0) and TB-500 (S2.3) are named on WADA’s list. KPV is not.

paragraphs: The three peptides in this lane have the same new status and very little human research behind it. On October 30, 2026, HHS said it will not take enforcement action against licensed pharmacies and physicians that compound [[/bpc-157|BPC-157]], [[/tb-500|TB-500]] and [[/kpv|KPV]], among six peptides, as long as every condition in its notice is met. None of the three is FDA approved for any use.

BPC-157 has the most human data, and it is small: five published studies, about 80 people, none longer than two weeks. The largest was a 2005 colitis trial of 53 people given an enema, reported only as a conference abstract; its result was not statistically significant. FDA’s scientists found no human studies using the routes people actually use: by mouth, under the skin, in the nose or on the skin.

TB-500 has less. FDA’s 2026 review found no study in which it was given to people, and no animal toxicity studies at all. Since then one case report has described three dental patients who got TB-500 mixed with BPC-157 and other drugs, so no single ingredient’s effect can be separated. KPV has no published human study of any kind; everything known about it comes from mice, rabbits and cells.

Registered trials do not change the picture yet. A Phase 2 trial of BPC-157 for hamstring strain, sponsored by Hudson Biotech, was registered in February 2026 and is recruiting, with no results. The only ClinicalTrials.gov record naming TB-500 describes itself as “a fictional study” and “an example” record. Its sponsor is the same company, Hudson Biotech. ClinicalTrials.gov lists no trial of KPV.

The HHS policy is enforcement discretion. It names set routes for each peptide, requires a patient-specific prescription, a single listed ingredient, and a bulk substance from an FDA-registered maker with a valid certificate of analysis, and asks for serious adverse events to be reported to FDA. It does not cover blends, outsourcing facilities, or products sold as research chemicals or supplements. It does not make any of them FDA approved, and HHS may revise or withdraw it. FDA’s own scientists had recommended against all three; its advisory committee voted 8 to 6, with one abstention, for each, as reported by Healio.

Sport has its own rules. WADA’s 2026 list names BPC-157 under S0, non-approved substances, and TB-500 under S2.3, growth factors; both are banned at all times. KPV is not named. S0 bans any substance with no current government approval for human use, but whether WADA applies that to KPV was not confirmed.

pull.quote: we did not identify data, such as clinical studies, on the use of TB-500 in humans.
